svg.title: Objectives and Optimization Architecture
svg.desc: Overview of the atlas. The brain exchanges observations and actions with the world, which it experiences from a first-person view and through hearing, touch, proprioception and interoception. Four learning systems build and use its world model: the cerebral cortex learns a hierarchical generative model by self-supervised prediction, the hippocampus binds episodes in one shot and replays them, the basal ganglia learn by reinforcement which actions to select, and the cerebellum calibrates fast forward models of movement. Neuromodulators set gain, learning rate and mode. The system is driven by superordinate objectives (minimizing risk and ambiguity, compression progress, empowerment, and models of minds) and is built from neurons, synapses, glia, plasticity, neuromodulators and neural representations.
